subject: Dedicated allocation design + activation velocity: Helios Therapeutics
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lang <ava.lang@heliostx.com>, Helios Procurement <procurement@heliostx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated allocation design + activation velocity: Helios Therapeutics

Hi Ava / James —

Following our workshop last week, attached is a concise set of reservation options tailored to the Helios ML serving profile you shared (95th percentile seq len ~512, average concurrency 42 reqs/sec, peak batch bursts for nightly retrain). High level — three candidate paths depending on your desired risk/cost tradeoff:

1) Transit Pilot (short ramp)
- Minimum: 8 dedicated GPUs reserved
- Peak cap: designed to scale to 24 GPUs within 12 weeks (triggered by usage thresholds)
- Warm-start credits: 100 GPU-hours to accelerate model warm-up
- Use-case: validate end-to-end inference latency and KV cache effectiveness before committing
- Approx list: $X / GPU-hr (see attached)

2) Production Anchor (recommended for v1 launch)
- Minimum floor: 32 dedicated GPUs (SLA-backed lane)
- Elastic burst: additional 20% capacity available for 90-day windows subject to availability
- Ramp cadence: start at 32 -> 64 in month 2 -> 96 in month 4 -> 128 by month 6 (contingent on usage ramp milestones)
- Warm-start credits: 500 GPU-hours + pre-warm scheduling to reduce cold-start token latency
- Monitoring: per-token latency SLOs, cost dashboards, and auto-fallback to compatible model variant on saturation

3) Anchored Enterprise (long-term predictable throughput)
- Minimum: 64 GPUs committed
- Structured ramp: two-phase activation with fixed monthly increases and priority hardware allocation
- Business terms: 12–24 month commit with volume pricing and on-call support SLA

Notes / tradeoffs:
- Minimums are set to preserve predictable throughput and KV cache efficiency; very small floors (<8 GPUs) materiallly increase per-token cost and cold-start risk.
- We can compress the Production ramp if you accept higher initial burn (additional warm-start credit or prepay).
- All options include network isolation and customer KMS integration if you choose the Private option.

Next steps: please indicate which path (Pilot / Production / Anchored) fits your go-to-market timeline and whether you want us to accelerate ramp timing. I attached a spreadsheet with a week-by-week activation velocity and estimated burn. If you prefer, we can jump on a 30-min call to pick a lane and convert to a short-term addendum + DocuSign.

Attachments: Helios_RSV_Options_v4.xlsx, Mutual_Action_Plan_helios.docx

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
Redwood Inference
From: Ava Lang <ava.lang@heliostx.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Helios Procurement <procurement@heliostx.com>
Cc: James O'Neill <j.oneill@heliostx.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 12:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated allocation design + activation velocity: Helios Therapeutics

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few clarifying questions before we pick a lane: 

- The warm-start credits: how are those consumed? Are they applied to GPU-hours or to a separate warm-up window that doesn't count against committed hours?
- For the Production Anchor, is that 20% burst guaranteed or best-effort? We need to understand worst-case latency during heavy scoring windows.
- We will need SOC2 evidence and a short list of IP ranges for allowlisting for our VPC peering team. Can you include that with the contract package?

Also — can we accelerate the Production ramp to reach 96 GPUs by month 3 instead of month 4? Our product launch moved up. If that requires a different billing cadence or an upfront prepay, tell me what you'd need. 

Happy to take a 30-min call Friday if that helps.

Best,
Ava Lang
Head of ML Infrastructure, Helios Therapeutics
ava.lang@heliostx.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated allocation design + activation velocity: Helios Therapeutics (internal note)

Kim / Ben — quick ops note on the ramp ask (Ava wants 96 by month 3):

- If we accelerate to 96 by month 3, recommend we: (a) increase warm-start credits to 800 GPU-hrs, (b) reserve an extra 10% buffer (warm standby) for first 8 weeks to avoid tail latency spikes during KV-cache warming, and (c) commit to a rolling prewarm schedule to align model retrains with lower-traffic windows.
- Cost impact: aggressive ramp increases 1st-quarter burn by ~37% vs. our standard cadence, but the unit price can be softened with a 12-month commitment or a prepay tranche.
- Hardware note: we'll need to lock a priority placement window in the deployment queue for the first two activation weeks — suggest we mark it as "priority activation" in the SOW to ensure earliest available nodes.

I'll draft a short clause for the MvA and a pricing appendix we can attach.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lang <ava.lang@heliostx.com>, Helios Procurement <procurement@heliostx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated allocation design + activation velocity: Helios Therapeutics

Ava / James — thanks, answered inline and updated attachments. See new attachment (Helios_RSV_Options_v4.xlsx) and SOC2_Readme.pdf. Short answers: 

- Warm-start credits: consumed as GPU-hours dedicated to prewarming sessions and do not count against the committed-month usage; they are applied as a one-time credit during the pre-launch window per the MvA.
- Production Anchor burst: the 20% is a contractual burst window (best-effort supply defined in SOW) with firm fallback — if burst cannot be granted due to capacity constraints, traffic will be routed to a lower-cost compatible variant and we will notify you with 15-min alerts. We include per-token latency monitoring and an escalation path.
- SOC2 / IP ranges: attached SOC2_Readme.pdf with links to the security package. IP ranges for peering are in the Drive link; I'll add them to the DocuSign package.

About acceleration to month 3: we can meet 96 GPUs by month 3 under Production if Helios signs the 12-month commitment with a 30% upfront prepayment for the accelerated tranche. Karthik's team recommends the extra warm-start credit I noted above; we'll include the priority activation clause in the SOW.

Next step: if you confirm "Production — accelerated to 96 by month 3" we'll send a short amendment and DocuSign link for the prepay tranche and schedule a 30-min alignment call. Friday 10:00 or 15:00 PT work for me.

Attachments: Helios_RSV_Options_v4.xlsx, SOC2_Readme.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan_helios.docx

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ava Lang <ava.lang@heliostx.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Helios Procurement <procurement@heliostx.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated allocation design + activation velocity: Helios Therapeutics

Thanks — we want to proceed with: Production (accelerated to 96 GPUs by month 3) subject to the 12-month commitment + 30% prepay. Please send the amended Annex + DocuSign and include the SOC2 artifact and IP ranges. Also add the priority activation clause to the SOW. Once procurement has the DocuSign, we'll route internally for signature.

Let's take Friday 10:00 PT for a quick call to confirm activation windows.

—
Ava
